thread:
maria: Heads up — after tonight's kernel-6.4.12 rollout in us-west-2 we're seeing multiple A100 nodes with P2P disabled. Batch/allreduce jobs hang with NCCL errors like 'unreachable peer' and long retries. Any oncall available?
lee: Seeing the same in ampere-rack-17. Quick check: `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows unexpected topology changes between GPU pairs, some links reporting as SYS instead of NVLINK.
raj: dmesg on one host shows PCI BAR1 resizing logs right after the kernel init: 'BAR1 window reduced, BAR1 truncated to 256MiB' — that smells like a BAR1 sizing/ACS interaction with the new kernel PCI changes.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: kernel/6.4.12 rollout completed in region us-west-2 at 1818003200.
ciara: Quick hypothesis: the kernel's PCI/ACS changes combined with our driver variant are causing BAR1/peeraccess to be negotiated down, which disables P2P. NCCL then falls back poorly. Short mitigations: (1) schedule affected jobs off those racks, (2) set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 or NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=1 in job env to force CPU-mediated collectives (slower but keeps jobs alive).
maria: Can someone confirm the exact env var we set for internal training jobs? We need a short play to stop the immediate failures.
lee: We tested `export NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` on a failing container and the allreduce completed (slower) — confirmed as a viable short-term workaround. Will push a runscript change for active runs.
raj: Ops note: rolling jobs to other regions will increase egress/cost — need to be mindful. If we keep workers without P2P for many hours, cluster spend could jump ~1.5-2x for big multi-GPU jobs.
ciara: Cost + reliability tradeoff decision required: rollback kernel or continue with mitigations. Rollback avoids perf hit but is heavier operationally. Also: check if driver 535.x vs 525.x behaves differently with the kernel change.
maria: Proposed plan: hold further kernel rollouts, spin up canary nodes with previous kernel (6.3.x) next to affected racks, migrate in-flight jobs where possible, and roll back the rollout in the region if canary confirms.
lee: I'll open a tracking ticket with `lspci -vv` and `dmesg` excerpts and attach `nvidia-smi topo -m` outputs for a couple hosts. Adding the BAR1/resizing log lines and kernel package version.
raj: Driver team — any chance to force BAR1 mapping or override ACS flags from userspace as a rapid mitigation? That would be less disruptive than a full kernel rollback if safe.
devops-oncall: Driver/infra update: forcing BAR1/ACS from userspace is risky across kernel ABI changes. We're prioritizing a rollback of 6.4.12 in us-west-2 with a 90-minute rollback window — ETA ~1818004020. Meanwhile we'll patch job templates to set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE for new runs targeted to affected pools and prevent autoscaler from placing GPUs into those racks.
maria: Thanks — I'll update customers, mark the incident, and coordinate the rollback window. Please add any test commands or logs to the ticket so we can write a postmortem with remediation/action items. :white_check_mark:
ciara: After rollback/patch, follow-up items: reproduce in a small lab with the same kernel/driver combo, validate BAR1 sizing across kernel builds, and add a canary gate for PCI/driver interactions in future rollouts.
lee: Also recommended: add a runtime health check (NCCL quick topology/allreduce probe) as part of node join gating so we detect P2P regressions earlier.
maria: Agreed — opening a follow-up RFC for gating and adding cost impact estimates to the postmortem. Thanks all.
